{{short description|French mathematician (born 1948)}}
'''Bernard Maurey''' (born 1948)<ref>{{cite book|author=Pietsch, Albrecht|title=History of Banach spaces and linear operators|publisher=Springer|year=2007|page=653|isbn=978-0-8176-4596-0 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MMorKHumdZAC&pg=PA653}}</ref> is a French mathematician who deals with [[functional analysis]] and especially the theory of [[Banach space]]s.

He received in 1973 his Ph.D. from the [[University Paris VII]] (Denis Diderot) under [[Laurent Schwartz]] with thesis ''Théorèmes de factorisation pour les opérateurs linéaires à valeurs dans les espaces L<sup>p</sup>''.<ref>{{cite book|title=Probability in Banach Spaces: Isoperimetry and Processes|author=Ledoux, Michel|author2=Talagrand, Michel|authorlink2=Michel Talagrand|publisher=Springer|year=2002|page=472|isbn=978-3-540-52013-9 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cyKYDfvxRjsC&pg=PA472}}</ref><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=73867}}</ref> Maurey is a professor at the University of Paris VII and a member of the [[CNRS]]'s ''Laboratoire d'Analyse et de Mathématiques Appliquées'' of the [[University of Marne-la-Vallée]]. He was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1974 in [[Vancouver]].

He introduced stable Banach spaces in 1981 with [[Jean-Louis Krivine]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Krivine, Jean-Louis|author2=Maurey, Bernard|title=Espaces de Banach stables|journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]|volume=39|issue=4|year=1981|pages=273–295|doi=10.1007/BF02761674|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Guerre-Delabriere, Sylvia|title=Classical sequences in Banach spaces|series=Monographs and textbooks in pure and applied mathematics, vol. 166|publisher=CRC Press|year=1992|page=108|isbn=978-0-8247-8723-3 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=S14-Kut97MEC&pg=PA108}}</ref> In 1992, with [[Timothy Gowers]], Maurey resolved the "unconditional basic sequence problem" in the theory of Banach spaces, by showing that not every infinite-dimensional Banach space has an infinite-dimensional subspace that admits an [[Schauder basis|unconditional Schauder basis]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-1993-1201238-0|author=Gowers, William Timothy|authorlink=Timothy Gowers|author2=Maurey, Bernard|title=The unconditional basic sequence problem|journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society|volume=6|issue=4|year=1993|pages=851–874|arxiv=math/9205204}}</ref>
